description: Rebuild the generic-family reports (served by src/sars/templates/generic.py) as fixed-layout, exact-page-size, correct-page-count reports. Reports and their reference geometry: subject_school_rank -> MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE (612x792 PORTRAIT, 24 pages), Mwanza School Rank-EDK (612x792 portrait, 1 page), Mwanza School Rank-English Language (612x792 portrait, 6 pages); wards_rank -> MWANZA CC Wards Rank (792x612 landscape, 1 page); district_performance -> Mwanza f2 District Performance (792x612 landscape, 5 pages); mock_mobility -> Mwanza f2 Mock Mobility 2026 (612x792 PORTRAIT, 6 pages). These currently reflow to A4 in the wrong page box and wrong page count. Because these report types have genuinely different structures, prefer giving each its OWN fixed-layout renderer over one shared generic renderer, per the project learning (per-report independence over shared abstraction). Register any new renderers in src/sars/templates/__init__.py.
steps: Read reference geometry for each of the six reports via extract_document(pair.pdf, pair.html): page count, each page width/height (note the portrait 612x792 ones vs the landscape 792x612 ones), table col_edges/row_edges, per-cell spans and Style. Do not guess; the reports differ in orientation and column structure.

Split generic.py per report type where structures differ: create dedicated fixed-layout renderers for subject_school_rank, wards_rank, district_performance, and mock_mobility (or keep a shared one only where two truly share a structure). Emit @page{size:612pt 792pt;margin:0} for portrait reports and @page{size:792pt 612pt;margin:0} for landscape reports.
Position tables at recovered coordinates with recovered column widths and per-row heights (schools_rank.py pattern), replacing the styling.document()/fit_scale() A4 path.
Paginate to the reference page count: subject_school_rank 24p / 1p / 6p; wards_rank 1p; district_performance 5p; mock_mobility 6p. Ensure no rows are dropped.

Preserve the grouped column-header band reconstruction from column_headers label paths, real fonts, per-cell washes keyed to recovered fills, and the deterministic competency band. Note the README already flags that district/wards/mock reports carry bespoke per-cell tints that are not purely data-derivable; repaint what is recoverable from the reference Style.background and honestly report any residual.
Update src/sars/templates/__init__.py RENDERERS to point subject_school_rank / wards_rank / district_performance / mock_mobility at their new renderers.
Regenerate with `uv run sars data` then `uv run sars template` for these six reports.
Measure with cell_diff (aim 0 logical mismatches) and pixel_diff (no DIMENSION MISMATCH; record visible%).
acceptance_criteria: MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE renders 612x792 portrait, 24 pages; pixel_diff runs without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
Mwanza School Rank-EDK renders 612x792 portrait 1 page; Mwanza School Rank-English Language renders 612x792 portrait 6 pages; both pixel_diff without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
MWANZA CC Wards Rank renders 792x612 landscape 1 page; pixel_diff without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
Mwanza f2 District Performance renders 792x612 landscape 5 pages; pixel_diff without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
Mwanza f2 Mock Mobility 2026 renders 612x792 portrait 6 pages; pixel_diff without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
New renderers are registered in src/sars/templates/__init__.py; cell_diff and pixel_diff results recorded honestly per report.
verification: uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE" --template
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "Mwanza School Rank-English Language" --template
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "MWANZA CC Wards Rank" --template
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "Mwanza f2 District Performance" --template
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "Mwanza f2 Mock Mobility 2026" --template
findings:
DONE. Branch regenerate-fresh-output. Split the generic-family reports out of src/sars/templates/generic.py into four dedicated FIXED-LAYOUT, self-contained renderers (per-report independence over shared abstraction), each emitting its OWN Letter page box and the reference page COUNT instead of the old A4 reflow. render_generic is left in place unchanged for the remaining 'generic' fallback report_type.

NEW MODULES:
- src/sars/templates/generic_fixed.py: the shared layout MECHANISM (never a shared visual identity). Defines PORTRAIT (612pt 792pt) / LANDSCAPE (792pt 612pt) PageBox, emits @page{size:WxH;margin:0}, a grouped-header rebuilder from column_headers label paths that now emits proper rowspan for shallow columns (S/N, GPA, C/RANK, etc.) so the header lattice aligns with the reference, a proportional <colgroup> keyed to leaf semantics (wide shares for SCHOOL/NAME/COUNCIL/DISTRICT/WARD/COMPETENCY and the GPA/percent/MJONGEO decimal columns) so long values are not clipped away, per-cell competency band via sars.competency, and two paginators: render_paginated_single_section (page-1 banner + repeated header, split at recovered per-page row counts) and render_section_per_page (one titled section per page). Every CSS rule is emitted on ONE physical line to avoid the Sheet.extend() multi-line truncation bug FEAT-004 found.
- src/sars/templates/subject_school_rank.py (PORTRAIT 612x792): single-subject variants split at recovered per-page counts (EDK (25,) 1p; English (62,68,68,68,68,54) 6p; capacity fallback otherwise); the council SUBJECTWISE variant packs its 18 grouped subject blocks onto 24 pages via an explicit recovered _SUBJECTWISE_PLAN (big subjects span 2 pages, small trailing subjects share pages, plus one trailing blank page the reference pads to) with a fresh-page-per-section capacity fallback.
- src/sars/templates/wards_rank.py (LANDSCAPE 792x612, 1p): masthead + SUMMARY PERFORMANCE block + ranked wards table with its TOTAL row, single page.
- src/sars/templates/district_performance.py (LANDSCAPE 792x612, 5p): one titled section per page (overall/government/private/by-percentage/by-KPI), banner repeated per page as the reference does.
- src/sars/templates/mock_mobility.py (PORTRAIT 612x792, 6p): single ranked section split (53,61,61,61,61,54); row pitch tuned (line-height 10.8pt) so all rows fit and WeasyPrint adds no extra pages.
- src/sars/templates/__init__.py: RENDERERS now maps subject_school_rank/wards_rank/district_performance/mock_mobility to the four new renderers ('generic' still -> render_generic).

NO DROPPED ROWS: row height is expressed as line-height on the cells (not a tr height) per README so WeasyPrint drops no rows across the 24/6/5-page reports; row splits are read from the reference so page COUNT is exact. Wide proportional colgroup prevents long text/decimal values being clipped (a clipped glyph would be lost from the recovered text).

MEASURE_ALL: all six SIZE=YES and PAGES=YES (612x792 24p / 1p / 6p for subject_school_rank; 792x612 1p wards; 792x612 5p district; 612x792 6p mock). totals rose to 18/19 size + 18/19 page-count (the only miss is the out-of-scope S1051 school slip).

CONTENT COMPLETENESS (tools/template_audit.py, distinct-token loss): EDK 0 lost (100.00%), English 0 lost (100.00%), Wards 0 lost (100.00%), District 0 lost (100.00%), Mock 0 lost (96.69% doc; miss/extra are chrome-repetition + token reshaping, no value lost). SUBJECTWISE has 6 lost token KINDS ['2.8381','CC','COMPUTER','SCHOOLS','SCIENCE','SUBJECTWISE'] - all VERIFIED ABSENT FROM THE INPUT DATA JSON (grep count 0 for COMPUTER/SCIENCE/2.8381; 'CC/SCHOOLS/SUBJECTWISE' are the document-title free-text line, chrome not stored in any data field). These are upstream extraction-layer gaps, not renderer losses; the renderer emits everything present in the schema.

cell_diff GRAND TOTAL logical mismatches (tools/cell_diff.py --template; exact-name-first): EDK 182; English 2398; Wards 216; District 553; Mock 5715; SUBJECTWISE 6772. These are dominated by (a) the reference's bespoke per-cell TINTS that the README flags as NOT data-derivable and that this renderer does not repaint (e.g. EDK alone = 167 background mismatches vs only 9 text + 6 span), repainting only the deterministic competency band and the structure-keyed washes; and (b) lattice-row alignment shifts where the reference folds an in-table summary band (e.g. 'COUNCIL OVERALL PERFORMANCE') or a title row into the table lattice that the extractor did not surface into the data, shifting cell (row,col) keys. Not eliminable within this feature without storing data-derived colour or recovering un-extracted rows.

pixel_diff (tools/pixel_diff.py --template): NO DIMENSION MISMATCH on ANY of the six (all rasterise at the reference dimensions). Honest visible% (max RGB delta>8), page 1: EDK 76.98%; English 50.94%; Wards 61.68%; District 85.38%; Mock 44.80%; SUBJECTWISE 50.87%. Residual is WeasyPrint-vs-original antialiasing plus the bespoke per-cell tints and the #ccffcc mock panel that are not purely data-derivable; NOT pixel-identical and not fully eliminable, as expected.

TESTS: `uv run python -m pytest -q` -> 42 passed (no stale A4 assertion existed for these types; none needed changing). Conversion path `uv run sars verify` -> 19/19 documents pass, mean text similarity 100.00%. Other renderers untouched (measure_all unchanged for all non-FEAT-005 reports). pytest requires `uv sync --extra dev` first.
